content.text: Welcome to Setpoint
Setpoint adds the machines of a real process plant: pumps, tanks, control valves, controllers, generators and a control room.
**Easy by default.** Every machine works the moment you place it. Pumps start by themselves and controllers find their own valve.
**Depth if you want it.** Underneath runs real physics: pump curves, cavitation and PID control. Ignore it, or dive in.
**At the heart of it: P&IDs.** Build a plant, then draw it as a real P&ID with a blank P&ID sheet. See the next chapter.
Right-click any Setpoint machine with an empty hand to read its status.
Using this book
Use the arrows to turn pages, or Contents to jump to a chapter. Hover an item to see its name.
Lost the book? Craft a new one:
Draw your plant
A P&ID (piping and instrumentation diagram) is how real plants are drawn: every pump, tank, valve and instrument as a symbol, with the pipes between them. In Setpoint you draw one of your own plant.
**1.** Take a blank P&ID and right-click the ground at one corner of your plant.
**2.** Look at the opposite corner: the box shows in the world, ten blocks high. Right-click it.
**3.** You get a P&ID. Right-click it to give it a name and read the drawing.
The drawing always goes ten blocks up from the lowest corner, so just pick the corners on the ground. Up to 32 x 24 blocks. Sneak-right-click the air to start over. Each drawing uses up one sheet.
Reading a P&ID

A circle with an arrow is a **pump**, pointing where it pumps. A box with liquid is a **tank**. A bow tie is a **valve**: with a dome on top for a control valve, a T for a hand valve, filled in when it is shut.
Bubbles are **instruments**: L for level, F for flow. A circle in a square is a **DCS controller**; dashed amber lines are its signal wiring to its valve and transmitter.
Hover any symbol on the drawing to see its tag.
Live on the console
Right-click a DCS console with your P&ID to put it in. The **P&ID** tab of the console now shows your drawing, live.
Running equipment turns **cyan**, tanks fill up to their real level, amber needs attention and alarms flash **magenta**. Grey means the console cannot see it: gone, or more than 32 blocks away.
Scroll to zoom, drag to move, click a symbol for its trend. **VALUES** writes the numbers on the drawing, **EJECT** gives the P&ID back.
On the wall
A **P&ID board** shows a P&ID big on the wall of your control room, live, like a mimic board. Place boards side by side and below each other: together they make one panel, up to 8 x 6 blocks.
Right-click any board of the panel with a P&ID. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to take it back. A board sees the plant within 32 blocks, like a console.

**Work it from the wall.** Look at a symbol: its tag, status and value show above your hotbar. Right-click it: a controller opens its faceplate, a pump starts or stops, a hand or drain valve opens or shuts, anything else reports its status.
A comparator next to the panel gives the number of alarms on the drawing: hook up a lamp or a bell. A panel with a P&ID glows, so it lights up your control room.
A tank that holds its own level
**1.** Craft two tanks, some pipes, a centrifugal pump, a control valve, a DCS controller and a Stirling engine.
**2.** Fill the first tank with water buckets, or pipe in endless water from a water intake in a river.
**3.** Stand on the side of the full tank and place the pump: its suction faces you. Connect both sides with pipes.
**4.** Put the Stirling engine against the pump and give it coal. The pump starts by itself.
**5.** Put a control valve in the line to the second tank, and a DCS controller against that tank.
**6.** Done. The controller finds the valve and holds the tank at 50 %. Right-click it to change the setpoint.
Bonus: a DCS console within 32 blocks shows the whole plant on one screen.
Pipe
Copper pipe connects itself to tanks, pumps, valves and boilers. Longer runs mean more friction and less flow. A run can be 512 pipes long.
Tank

Holds 16 buckets of one fluid. The sight glass shows the level, in the colour of the liquid. Click it with a bucket, or open it and use the bucket slots: full bucket in at the top, empty bucket out below.
**Stack tanks** to make one tall tank: liquid settles to the bottom, and the level, comparators and controllers count the whole column.
A comparator next to a tank gives a redstone signal from 0 (empty) to 15 (full).
Drum and IBC

Containers you can carry. A **drum** holds 4 buckets and stands one and a half blocks high; an **IBC** holds 20 and takes two by two by two blocks. A real drum holds 200 kg and an IBC 1000 kg; here 1 kg is 20 mB. You see the liquid through the white tote of an IBC.
An IBC reaches to your left and away from you from where you place it, so leave room. Pipes fit on any of its blocks.

**Colours.** Right-click a drum with any dye to paint it. An IBC is white, or black with black dye (a black one keeps the light out, so you cannot see the liquid). They keep their colour when you carry them away.
They work like a tank with buckets, pipes, pumps and controllers. Break one and the liquid goes along in the item; place it somewhere else and it is all still there.
Gases

Gas is counted like liquid, in mB, but **at 1 bar**. Squeeze more into the same room and the pressure goes up: twice the gas, twice the bar. Gas flows by itself from high pressure to low, through **gas pipes**, to everything on the line.
Four gases so far: **hydrogen**, **oxygen**, **nitrogen** and **steam**. Gas pipes never join liquid pipes or tanks.

The **electrolyser** splits water into hydrogen (out on your left) and oxygen (out on your right), two to one. It needs power and water at the back or from below. Oxygen with nowhere to go is let into the air.
The **nitrogen generator** takes nitrogen out of the air, with only power. It comes out on your left.

Both fill their outlet up to **10 bar**, then wait until something takes the gas. A **boiler** gives its steam to a gas pipe on top, and a **steam turbine** takes steam from a gas pipe on any side, so they no longer have to touch.

A **gas cylinder** holds one gas up to 200 bar; its shoulder shows which. Pipes join it on top and its sides. A pressure transmitter reads it and a safety valve protects it. Break it and the gas goes along in the item.

To go past 10 bar, use a **gas compressor**. Like the pump, its suction is on the side that faced you and its discharge on the far side. It draws from the fullest vessel on the suction line and fills the emptiest one on the discharge line, up to 200 bar. The higher the gas coming in, the more it moves; the harder it squeezes, the more power it takes.

Using the gases. A **fuel cell** turns hydrogen (left) and oxygen (right) back into power, 24 FE/t, and water: with an electrolyser and a gas sphere you can store power. Pipe **oxygen** into the back of a **boiler** and its coal lasts half as long again.

The **ammonia reactor** makes ammonia, the fifth gas, from nitrogen (left) and hydrogen (right), out on top. It wants pressure: full speed with its feed at 100 bar, so put a compressor on its feed lines. In a **fertilizer mixer**, ammonia (left) and bone meal make **NPK fertilizer**: use it on a crop and every crop in the three by three around it grows up at once.

For a lot of gas there is the **gas sphere**: a round pressure vessel on eight columns, like the spheres that hold propane and hydrogen on a real plant. It takes eight by eight blocks and is ten high, has 220 B of room and is built for **16 bar**, so it holds up to 3520 B of gas. Place it with one block: that block is its valve station at the front, where gas pipes join. It reaches four blocks to your left, three to your right and eight away from you.
Climb the caged ladder in the front-right corner and cross the bridge to the platform on top. A pressure transmitter or safety valve works against any block of it.
Pallet racking

Store loaded pallets up high with the forklift. Stand **rack uprights** in rows, with two blocks between them for each bay. At each level, lay **rack beams** two by two between the uprights: they sit in the top of the block. Drive the forklift up with a pallet, raise it over the beams and lower it: it sets the pallet down on them. Leave three blocks between levels for a pallet with drums.
Factory blocks

To build round your plant: **steel grating** (a thin see-through floor that lies in the bottom or the top of a block, like a slab), **grating stairs**, a yellow **handrail** (it stands on the side you look towards; place another in the same block for a corner), a **caged ladder**, a **steel I-beam** for columns and girders, **checker plate**, **hazard stripes**, **corrugated steel** cladding and an **industrial lamp**.
For a platform: put grating in the top half of the blocks, so it lies level with the floor around it, and handrails on the block above along its edges.
Oil

A **pumpjack** pumps crude oil out of the ground, anywhere. Place it with one block: that is the **wellhead**, where the crude oil comes out to a pipe, and the pumpjack stands four blocks long behind it. Give it power (30 FE/t) on any of its blocks and it nods: 10 mB of crude oil a tick, slowly and for ever.

The **distillation column** splits crude oil the way a refinery does: 5% LPG (a gas), 20% naphtha, 15% kerosene, 30% diesel and 30% residue. It is three wide, four deep and eleven high; place it with one block, the **feed** (crude oil in) in the middle of the front row. Every nozzle faces the front: **steam in** (from a boiler, through a gas pipe) on the left of the front row and **residue out** on the right; **diesel**, **kerosene** and **naphtha** out up the front of the column; **cooling water in** (left) and **LPG out** (right) at the top. Right-click a nozzle to see what it is. It takes up to 20 mB of crude oil a tick, and half as much steam and cooling water.

Crude oil and naphtha give off **vapour**: in an ordinary tank they slowly get less. Put a gas pipe with **nitrogen** on top of the tank to blanket them, or keep them in a floating roof tank, whose roof floats right on the liquid.
The **diesel generator** burns your own diesel: 80 FE/t for 4 mB a tick, the strongest power in the mod.
Flare stack

Where a plant burns the gas it cannot keep: a stack **forty blocks high** in a red and white derrick, the tallest thing in the mod. Place it with one block: that is the **ignition panel**, with the knock-out drum behind it and the tower behind that. It is seven blocks wide and reaches ten blocks away from you, so clear the space first.

Three gas lines join the panel. The **flare header** at the front: everything that goes to the flare. **Pilot gas** on your left: a little LPG or hydrogen keeps the pilot flame alight. **Steam** on your right, blown into the flame so LPG burns without smoke. Right-click the panel to light it.

Gas reaches the flare two ways. A **safety valve** with a gas pipe on its outlet blows off into the header instead of into the air. And the flare takes the excess off every vessel on its header that stands above its **set pressure** (sneak-right-click: 2, 5, 8 or 12 bar), so a column whose LPG has nowhere to go keeps running.

Hydrogen, ammonia and LPG burn: the more gas, the bigger the flame, up to sixteen blocks of fire that leans with the wind. Nitrogen and steam just go up the stack. Without pilot gas the flame goes out when nothing flows, and gas that comes then goes up unburnt: **FLARE OUT** on the console.
Climb the caged ladder up the inside of the tower to the three platforms; the top one is right under the tip. Do not stand in the flame.
Floating roof tank

The big storage tank of a tank farm, built from **Hookonium steel**: round, eight blocks across and six high, and it holds **8000 buckets**. Place it with one block: it reaches four blocks to your left, three to your right and eight away from you, so clear the space first.

Its top is open. The **roof** is a steel deck on a ring of pontoons that floats on the liquid: it rises as the tank fills and sinks as it empties, so you see the level from the rim. You can walk on the roof.
Climb the **caged ladder** in the front-right corner to the platform on the rim. From there the **rolling ladder** goes down to the roof. Walk into a ladder to climb it, like any ladder.
Pipes fit on any of its blocks; the nozzle at the front is where you placed it. Break it and the liquid goes along in the item, like a drum.
Pallet

A wooden pallet, two by two blocks, for up to **four drums**. Right-click it with a drum to load it; the drums keep their liquid and colour. Two or more get a green strap around them; three stand in a triangle.
An **IBC** fits on an empty pallet too: right-click the pallet with it. It stands on the wood instead of its own base, liquid and colour and all, so the pallet truck and the forklift can take it.
Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to take the last drum off. Break the pallet and everything drops.
Pallet truck
An electric pallet truck moves pallets, empty or loaded. Right-click the ground to set it down, then right-click it to take the tiller: it follows behind you as you walk, up steps and slabs.

Walk backwards to push its forks into a pallet: it picks the pallet up by itself. Press **CTRL** to set the pallet down; it waits a few seconds before it takes one up again. Hold **H** for the horn. Right-click again to let go.
Forklift

An electric forklift you drive. Right-click the ground to set it down and right-click it to get in. **W** and **S** drive, **A** and **D** steer. It steers with its **rear wheels**, like a real one: the back swings out when you turn, so leave room behind you.

The **arrow keys** raise and lower the forks, up to six blocks. Lower them to a pallet, drive them in and raise: the pallet comes up, drums and all. Lower it onto the ground, or onto anything solid higher up, and it stays there. With the load up high it only creeps along.
Hold **H** for the horn; sneak to get out.
Liquid runs downhill

Join two tanks with a pipe and the fuller one runs into the other until both stand at the same level, without a pump. A tank only lets liquid out while the level is above the pipe, so a pipe on a **higher block** of a tall tank is its **overflow**.
A water intake in a river feeds a lower tank all by itself. A control valve in a gravity line works too: a controller holds the level of the low tank.
Check valve
Lets liquid through one way only: the way its arrow points. It is placed pointing the way you look. Use it to stop a tank from running back, or a line from draining back when a pump stops.
Water intake
Endless water. Put it in a river, lake or the sea with at least two water source blocks next to it, and pipe it to a pump. Pumps can draw from it but not push into it.
Hand valve
Shuts a line by hand: right-click to open or shut. A redstone signal holds it shut. Like a real gate valve, the stem sticks out when it is open.
Drain valve

Place it on a tank and right-click to open it, or give it a redstone signal: the tank runs out onto the ground at 10 mB/t. Handy to empty a tank, and a steady load for a level controller to work against.
Pipe wrench
Click a pipe arm to cut or join that side, so two lines can run side by side. Click a machine to turn it a quarter. Sneak-click to pick a machine up.
Name your equipment

Every machine gets a tag like P-417. Write a new tag on a name tag in an anvil, like P-FEED, and right-click a pump, tank, boiler or any other machine with it: that is its tag now. The console, Jade and new P&IDs use it.
Centrifugal pump
Moves fluid from the tank on its suction side to the tank on its discharge side. Runs on FE: 4 to 20 FE/t, depending on how hard it works.
It starts by itself. A redstone signal stops it, like a stop button. **Sneak-right-click** it to turn that around: then it only runs while it gets a signal.
A comparator next to a pump gives 15 while it runs.
It works with tanks from other mods too: anything with fluid storage at the end of a pipe.

**Any liquid.** Pumps move lava and other mods' liquids too, and feel the difference: lava is three times as heavy and six times as thick, so it flows slower, takes more power, and cannot be sucked up from far below.
Cavitation
A pump needs enough pressure at its suction. Pull from a tank far below the pump, or through a long suction line, and it starts to **cavitate**: it crackles, loses flow and wears its impeller.
Fix the wear by right-clicking the pump with an iron ingot. Better: put the source tank higher, or the pump closer.
Right-click a pump to see flow, head, NPSH and wear.
Control valve
Throttles the flow in a pipe line. The bar on the actuator shows how far it is open. It lines up with the pipe you click on.
Sneak-click to choose its fail position: fail close (FC) or fail open (FO). A redstone signal trips it to that position.
DCS controller
Place it against a tank or boiler: it measures the level, finds the control valve and holds the level at 50 % in AUTO.
Right-click for the **faceplate**: change the setpoint, switch MAN / AUTO / CAS, pick a tuning, set HI and LO alarm limits.
Level transmitter
Measures the tank it is mounted on. Only needed when the controller has to stand somewhere else.
Flow control
Put a **flow transmitter** in a pipe line, like a valve, with a control valve in the same line. A DCS controller against the transmitter holds the flow: 50 % is 60 mB/t.
Field communicator
For wiring loops by hand: sneak-click transmitters and valves to collect them, then click a controller to link them.
Stirling engine
Your first power: 20 FE/t from anything that burns in a furnace. Coal is the sensible choice. One engine runs one pump.
Biogas generator
30 FE/t from anything a composter takes, plus rotten flesh. Richer waste runs longer.
Generators hold 20,000 FE, power every block they touch and only burn fuel while there is room for more.
Boiler
A coal-fired firebox under a water drum. It heats to 100 °C in about ten seconds, then makes 20 mB of steam per tick.
Steam turbine
Place it against a boiler. It spins up to 3000 rpm and makes 60 FE/t: three times the power per coal of a Stirling engine.
Keeping the boiler fed
Pump water in from a tank through a control valve, and put a DCS controller against the boiler. It holds the drum at 50 %.
Below 10 % drum level the burner trips, so a boiler can never run dry. A comparator reads the drum level.
Steam is pressure
A boiler keeps its steam in a closed drum, so the steam builds **pressure**. 400 mB of steam is one bar. The drum is built for **10 bar**; the turbine wants **6 bar** for full power.
When the turbine stops taking steam (its power has nowhere to go), the pressure climbs. Three things stand in the way, like on a real plant:
**1. The trip.** The burner stops at 9 bar and starts again at 7. On by default (config).
**2. The safety valve.** Put one on the drum. It pops open at 10 bar and blows off steam until the pressure is a bar lower.
**3. Nothing.** With the trip off and no safety valve, the drum bursts at 13 bar.
Sneak-right-click a safety valve to set it to 6, 8 or 10 bar. A comparator next to it sees it lift.
Pressure control

Put a **pressure transmitter** against the boiler, and a DCS controller against the transmitter. It becomes a **PIC**: it holds the pressure by turning the burner up and down, and the coal lasts longer at part fire.
Place the controller against the transmitter, not against the boiler: against the boiler it holds the drum level instead.
DCS console
Sees every Setpoint machine within 32 blocks, without any wiring.
**OVERVIEW** lists every tag with its status and value. Grey is normal, amber needs attention, magenta is an alarm.
**TRENDS** shows the last five minutes of a tag: click it on the overview. For a controller you see PV, SP and OP, and a button opens its faceplate.
**ALARMS** keeps the alarm list. A new alarm chimes and makes the console flash until you press **ACK**.
**P&ID** shows a P&ID of your plant, live: right-click the console with one to put it in.
Alarm states
**NEW**: not acknowledged yet. **ACK**: acknowledged, the problem is still there. **RTN**: the problem went away before anyone looked; acknowledge to clear it.
Overview screens

A video wall for the control room. Screens side by side and below each other make one wall, up to 8 by 6, that shows what the nearest console (within 32 blocks) sees. Right-click to switch page: **PLANT OVERVIEW** (a tile per tag), **ALARMS** (the alarm list) or **TRENDS** (the controllers first).
Alarm beacon

An amber rotating light with a horn. It turns and sounds while a console within 32 blocks has an alarm nobody acknowledged. ACK on the console stops it; right-click the beacon to silence only the horn.
Emergency stop

The **ESD** button. Push it in (right-click) and every pump, compressor, generator, boiler, turbine and machine within 32 blocks stops at once and stays stopped; the console shows them as **ESD** with an alarm. Pull it out (right-click again) to let the plant start. It gives a redstone signal while pressed.
Radios
Pick a radio from the charger (right-click) and the field operator calls in from the plant: how many units run, and what needs a look, worst first.
Furniture

**Control desks** join into one long desk; a **corner** turns the row. **Operator screens** stand on a desk. The **24-hour chair**: right-click to sit, sneak to get up. Put it down with its back to you, and you look at the desk.

To finish the room: a **raised floor** (with **vent** tiles), **ceiling panels** and **ceiling lights**, a **wall clock** with the time of day, a **filing cabinet** that holds as much as a barrel, a **printer**, a **coffee machine** (a cup gives a minute of speed and haste), a lit **exit sign** (right-click to turn its arrow), a **blast door** and **wired glass** for windows onto the plant.
Hookonium
A purple ore, as rare as diamond. Found deep in the Overworld, from y 16 down to bedrock, mostly in deepslate.
It needs a **diamond pickaxe**. It drops Raw Hookonium; Fortune gives more, Silk Touch gives the ore.
Nine ingots make a block, and back. Hookonium is saved for machines that are still being designed.
Pump curve
A pump makes 12 m of head with its discharge shut and up to 120 mB/t running free. Flow settles where the pump curve meets the pipe curve.
NPSH
Net positive suction head: the pressure margin at the suction. Available NPSH must beat required NPSH, or the pump cavitates.
PID control
Controllers run a PI loop with three tunings: SLOW, NORMAL and FAST. They pick reverse or direct action themselves.
Modes
MAN: you set the valve. AUTO: the controller holds its setpoint. CAS: another controller sets the setpoint. A bad measurement drops a controller to MAN.
